answer.location_description: A full-width horizontal stripe (grating) pattern covering essentially the whole crop from about row 2 to row 23. The stripes repeat every 4 rows (about 5 mm): bright rows 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 alternate with dark rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23. Its most visible parts are the image edges and the rows above and below the nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / banding artifact (texture pattern), not nodule anatomy
answer.mechanism: Two groups of structured layer-1 units carry the same 4-row grating with opposite phase, on top of their nodule templates. The 'ring/large' units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27 and 28 have negative biases and weight rows 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 positively and rows 2-3, 6-7, 14-15 (edges) and 18-19 negatively. They feed layer-2 units u1 (W3 +99) and u8 (W3 +58), e.g. u8 takes 3:+91, 8:+92, 24:+93, and u1 takes 28:+94, 27:+77, 21:+72. The always-on 'compact' units 2, 5, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 25, 29 and 30 have biases of about 70-99 and carry the inverted grating. They feed u9 (W3 -72) and u11 (W3 -64), e.g. u11 takes 14:+99, 18:+96, 25:+94. Together the network computes an approximately linear grating correlation. Brightness in the stripe phase of rows 4-5, 8-9 and so on raises the malignant pathway and lowers the benign one.
answer.evidence: The ring units are positive at full width in rows 4-5 and 8-9, for example unit 24 r5 '-6 42 46 45 41 ... 46 31 46', unit 8 r8 '28 12 24 23 ... 54 30 19 22 28 28', and unit 27 r5 all positive. They are positive again at full width in rows 16-17 and 20-21, e.g. unit 24 r20 '41 44 25 34', unit 27 r20 '41 18 48 28 40'. They are negative across rows 2-3 (about -20 to -50 in every column) and in rows 18-19. They are also negative at the edges of rows 14-15 (unit 8 r15 '-44 -11 -52', unit 28 r15 '-39 -44 -34 ... -42') and on the right of rows 6-7 (unit 3 r6 col 18 = -49, unit 28 r6 '-48 -48'). The compact units show exactly the opposite sign at the same rows: rows 2-3 at +40 to +60, rows 4-5 negative, rows 6-7 right side at +55 to +66, row 14-15 edges positive (unit 2 r14 '46 15 58 56', unit 5 r15 '57 45 63'), rows 18-19 positive, and row 22 positive. Lung nodules, vessels and chest wall have no reason to produce identical full-width bands with a fixed 4-row period at the image borders. This regularity points to an acquisition or overlay artifact (banding) that was correlated with the label. Unstructured units (0, 1, 4, 6, 7, 9-13, 15, 22, 23, 26, 31) look like noise and do not contribute a competing explanation.
answer.main_feature: The genuine signal is nodule size and extent. Compact units respond to a small bright core at rows 11-12, cols 10-13 with a dark surround and route to the benign side (u9, u11). Ring units respond to bright tissue spread over rows 7-17, cols 6-17 around the centre and route to the malignant side (u1, u8), so larger, more extensive nodules are called malignant.
